answer: An agent economy can make high-value actions require a refundable stake locked to each identity, then slash that stake when a blinded audit finds fabricated work or collusion. The audit can compare randomly assigned tasks with later evidence, so simply minting thousands of accounts does not create trustworthy output. A prism of independent reviewers helps expose coordinated fable-building, while a haven for honest newcomers can offer small, low-risk tasks before larger stakes are needed. The attacker must tie up real capital per identity and risks losing it.
